mbm-2701.clue: That loose thread is the trail home.
mbm-2701.quote: I embroidered the route to my grandparents' house on a quilt. I left a finger-length of thread loose at the gate. My nephew pulls it and says that's how he rings their bell.

mbm-2702.clue: I can park a boat by a buttercup.
mbm-2702.quote: Dad used to lay a buttercup on the dock and ask me to pull my canoe alongside without wetting it. The flower stayed dry at last. We put it in the middle of the lunch table.

mbm-2703.clue: Our tiebreaker belongs to the gulls.
mbm-2703.quote: We played beach volleyball till the shadow of the net reached our cooler. Tied score, empty water bottles. Two gulls landed on one side, so we awarded them the match and went swimming.

mbm-2704.clue: The first bead is the color of the bus.
mbm-2704.quote: My grandmother showed me a pattern for a beaded key loop. I used one yellow bead for the bus I caught to her house. When my keys rattle it gets me there all over again.

mbm-2705.clue: I smuggle my novels into the kitchen.
mbm-2705.quote: The cookbook stand holds my paperback open while the soup simmers. My father once glanced at it and asked why supper needed a detective in a blue overcoat.

mbm-2706.clue: We put the roof in an ordinary shoebox.
mbm-2706.quote: My climbing partner spent a winter working a steep overhang. I made a little cardboard copy with clay blobs for the holds. Over tea she moved two buttons up the miniature wall to show me the sequence. It finally made sense when I had the ceiling in my lap.

mbm-2707.clue: We have to pay the cat to cross the river.
mbm-2707.quote: We built a board-game bridge from craft sticks. Our cat parks a paw on it. The official toll is a scratch behind the ear and three minutes of very quiet negotiation.

mbm-2708.clue: I saw half a film on the roof of a car.
mbm-2708.quote: At a drive-in the sky was brighter than the screen until dusk. The shiny roof in front of us caught its reflection. For ten minutes the whole movie played upside down on blue paint.

mbm-2709.clue: My poles have two left mittens.
mbm-2709.quote: I knitted coloured covers for my ski pole grips, sewed both thumbs on the same side and used them anyway. I can spot my pair in a crowded lodge before the door closes.

mbm-2710.clue: My audience expects an egg to land sunny-side up.
mbm-2710.quote: Our cook cut an oval of white felt and stitched on a yellow circle to help me practice catching flat objects. It flies much better than an omelet. When it lands yellow side up after a show, he insists on serving breakfast.

mbm-2711.clue: My chess clock has a penny for a foot.
mbm-2711.quote: The park table tilts. I tuck a penny under the clock so it doesn't slide into my back rank. My opponent says it's the most useful piece I own and I can't disagree.

mbm-2712.clue: My mum still owns the first fish that escaped me.
mbm-2712.quote: I quilted a row of fish for Mum's picnic basket. One slipped off the pattern and swam over the edge, so I stitched its tail onto the underside. Now she makes people lift the basket before she gives them lunch.

mbm-2713.clue: I took a bite out of my blue-ribbon prize.
mbm-2713.quote: For our eating contest, the fair baker tied a twist of dough to my blue ribbon. I carried my trophy halfway home before I gave in and tried a corner.

mbm-2714.clue: The lift left a little star on my glove.
mbm-2714.quote: A snowflake landed on my dark mitten on the chairlift. My friend took its picture before it melted. Later our ski tracks crossed beneath the lift in the very same shape.

mbm-2715.clue: I draw a tiny island for my toes.
mbm-2715.quote: In beach volleyball I used to wander before serving. I draw a circle with my heel and keep one foot on my island. The tide only lets me own it for one game.

mbm-2716.clue: My paddle scratches out a poem.
mbm-2716.quote: I kayak along the reeds and listen to their stems brush the paddle blade. The sound changes as I turn upstream. Back on shore I try to write the rhythm down before my hands get dry.

mbm-2717.clue: I take a second breakfast for a cold rock.
mbm-2717.quote: There's a dark volcanic rock halfway up my hiking path that warms early in the sun. I sit on it with a sandwich and leave my other sandwich beside me to take the chill off.

mbm-2718.clue: I keep Saturdays in a biscuit tin.
mbm-2718.quote: I save the paper platform ticket from each trainspotting trip and sort them by weather. The foggy days go in the middle. You can open a tin in July and get a November morning.

mbm-2719.clue: I was a round dot at the center of the rainbow.
mbm-2719.quote: During one jump the sun was behind me and a little mist hung over the landing field. My canopy cast a tiny shadow with a ring of color around it. I raised a hand and the dot waved back before the mist thinned.

mbm-2720.clue: I sketched the back of the statue.
mbm-2720.quote: Everyone stood in front of the museum's proud stone lion. Round behind, its sculptor had carved one paw pad in astonishing detail. That's the lion in my notebook.

mbm-2721.clue: I go on the quiet Tuesday.
mbm-2721.quote: I visit the museum's wooden boats on Tuesday mornings when the floor is nearly empty. One creaks in its cradle as the room warms. It's the smallest sound a ship can make.

mbm-2722.clue: The stripes in my quilt aren't parallel.
mbm-2722.quote: I used favourite ties from three uncles. Their stripes all wander off in different directions. Put those uncles round one dinner table and their stories do exactly that.

mbm-2723.clue: I face my chair toward the wall.
mbm-2723.quote: An old whitewashed wall bounces warm sunlight into the shady end of our courtyard. I sit there with my book and the scent of basil. All the sunny afternoon I need fits on one page.

mbm-2724.clue: I collect dragons with bad knees.
mbm-2724.quote: The fanciest fantasy card in my deck shows a dragon limping home after battle. I traded two shiny champions for him. My opponents laugh till they see what he can do when he gets to rest.

mbm-2725.clue: Our TV marathon has a drawn curtain.
mbm-2725.quote: I stretched a piece of flannel on a string in front of the television. When everyone's pajamas are on, my niece pulls the curtain for the opening credits. Even the weather report gets a premiere.
